mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when GDPC1 YoY change is below -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when UNRATE exceeds 8% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of sustained industrial production contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock that erodes real purchasing power and increases financing costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed 3% simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 15% within a single month signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) when HOUST jumps above its 12-month MA by more than 15% in a single month.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) in the same month indicates a statistical anomaly likely due to data revision or misclassification, which historically precedes short-term market volatility and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls AND UNRATE rises in the same month (contradictory labor data)
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.20) following months with contradictory PAYEMS and UNRATE movements.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below -5% for three consecutive months signals a consumer deleveraging cycle, which reduces demand for durable goods and depresses corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < -5% annualized for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when RSAFS shows a persistent annualized decline below -5% for three months.
